name: EY
description: Targeted placement preparation for EY covering EY GDS Tech Assessment patterns and enterprise technical standards.
common_roles: Java Developer, Python Developer, Data Analyst, Software Engineer
hiring_rounds: Cognitive Online Test -> Technical Round -> Partner HR
aptitude_pattern: Numerical reasoning with financial tables + Inductive logic + Verbal comprehension
coding_pattern: 2 Practical coding exercises on Ledger reconciliation, Tax ID cleansing, Sliding window anomaly detection - 45 mins
technical_focus: Regulatory audit technology, SQL window functions (LEAD/LAG), database encryption (TDE), OWASP Top 10 mitigations
hr_tips: Align with EY purpose: 'Building a better working world', highest professional integrity standards
recommended_skills: SQL, Python, Java, PowerBI, Azure, Cyber Security, Data Analytics

questions.question: In EY GDS Tech Quantitative: A corporate tax client has a gross taxable income of $750,000. The corporate tax rate is 20% on the first $500,000 and 25% on the remaining income. What is the total corporate tax payable?
In an EY financial audit sample, an auditor examines 450 corporate invoices and finds discrepancies in 18 invoices. What is the discrepancy rate percentage?
Find the next number in the financial consulting sequence: 12, 25, 52, 107, ___?
An enterprise cloud project budget of $360,000 is shared among 3 delivery teams in the ratio 4:5:3. What is the budget allocation for the team with the largest share?
In EY Verbal Ability: Select the word that means 'strict adherence to an ethical code or moral principles in business consulting':
questions.explanation: 'Integrity' is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; moral uprightness.

questions.question: A software product depreciates in accounting value by 20% each year on diminishing balance. If purchased for $100,000, what is its book value at the end of 2 years?
In how many ways can an EY audit team of 4 consultants be selected from a pool of 8 qualified professionals?
A consulting consultant drives 120 km at 60 km/h and another 120 km at 40 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 240 km. Total time = 120/60 + 120/40 = 2 + 3 = 5 hours. Average speed = 240 / 5 = 48 km/h.

questions.question: In EY Syllogisms: Statements: 1. All financial statements are audited. 2. All audited documents are compliant. Conclusion: All financial statements are compliant.
questions.explanation: Transitive deduction: Financial statements -> Audited -> Compliant. Therefore, All financial statements are compliant follows unconditionally.

questions.question: A sum of money invested at simple interest yields $1,200 interest in 3 years at 5% per annum. What was the principal invested?
In an analytical test, 65% of candidates passed Section A, 70% passed Section B, and 15% failed both. What percentage of candidates passed BOTH sections?
questions.explanation: Total passed at least one = 100% - 15% = 85%. P(Both) = P(A) + P(B) - P(At least one) = 65% + 70% - 85% = 135% - 85% = 50%.

questions.question: If an automated ETL process takes 45 minutes to process 90,000 records, what is the processing throughput in records per second?
questions.explanation: Time in seconds = 45 * 60 = 2,700 seconds. Throughput = 90,000 / 2,700 = 33.33 records/sec.

questions.question: In EY Direction Logic: An auditor walks 20 meters North, turns Right and walks 30 meters, turns Right and walks 20 meters. How far is the auditor from the starting point?
questions.explanation: North and South cancel out (+20 - 20 = 0). Position is 30 meters directly East.

questions.question: What is the probability of selecting an odd number from the first 25 natural numbers (1 to 25)?
questions.explanation: Odd numbers: 1, 3, 5, ..., 25 (13 numbers). Total numbers = 25. Probability = 13/25 = 52%.

questions.question: A team of 6 analysts finishes an assurance report in 8 days. How many analysts are needed to finish the same report in 4 days?
questions.explanation: Work = 6 * 8 = 48 analyst-days. Analysts needed for 4 days = 48 / 4 = 12 analysts.

questions.question: Given two arrays of transactions ledgerA and ledgerB, return the symmetric difference: transaction amounts that exist in ledgerA or ledgerB but not in both.
questions.explanation: Count frequencies using HashMaps; collect elements where count in A != count in B, or set symmetric difference in O(N+M).

extra.title: Financial Ledger Reconciliation (EY GDS Tech)

questions.question: Given an array of raw tax ID strings containing erratic formatting (hyphens, spaces, lowercase characters), clean and standardize each tax ID to uppercase alphanumeric without separators.
questions.explanation: Use regex replaceAll('[^a-zA-Z0-9]', '') and toUpperCase() on each string in O(Total Chars).

extra.title: Cleanse and Standardize Tax IDs

questions.question: Given a stream of daily transaction amounts and a threshold multiplier, flag any transaction that is greater than 3 times the rolling average of the previous k days.
questions.explanation: Sliding window queue maintaining running sum of previous k elements; compare current element with 3 * (running_sum / k) in O(N).

extra.title: Sliding Window Financial Anomaly Detection

questions.question: Given a string representing a credit card number, return true if the number is valid according to the Luhn checksum algorithm.
questions.explanation: Traverse digits from right to left; double every second digit; subtract 9 if > 9; sum all digits; valid if sum % 10 == 0.

extra.title: Validate Credit Card Number (LUHN Algorithm)

questions.question: Given an array of transaction strings in the format 'Vendor:Category:Amount', aggregate and return the total spent per unique category.
questions.explanation: Split string by ':'; accumulate amounts into a HashMap<String, Integer> in O(N).

extra.title: Group Transactions by Vendor Category

questions.question: Given expected payments and received payments, determine if each payment matches the expected amount within an allowable rounding tolerance of 0.05.
questions.explanation: Check Math.abs(exp - recv) <= tol with precision rounding.

extra.title: Reconcile Invoices with Rounding Tolerances

questions.question: In forensic auditing, transactions between accounts can form circular wash trades (e.g. Account A -> B -> C -> A). Given V accounts and transaction edges, detect if any circular wash trade exists.
questions.explanation: Cycle detection in directed graph using DFS with recursion stack or Kahn's topological sort in O(V + E).

extra.title: Detect Circular Transactions in Auditing (Graph Cycle)

questions.question: Given an annual taxable income and tax bracket thresholds with corresponding progressive rates, calculate the total progressive tax payable.
questions.explanation: Iterate brackets; calculate taxable portion in current bracket; multiply by rate; accumulate in O(B).

extra.title: Calculate Compound Tax Brackets

questions.question: In EY regulatory audit and tax technology architectures, how do you enforce Database Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and secure key rotation using Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS?
questions.explanation: TDE encrypts database files, logs, and backups at rest using AES-256 with a Database Encryption Key (DEK). The DEK is protected by a Customer Managed Key (CMK) in HSM/Key Vault, rotated annually with automated re-wrapping.

questions.explanation: LAG() accesses prior row values; LEAD() accesses subsequent row values without self-joins. SUM() OVER with ORDER BY calculates running cumulative balance per account across time partitions.
